title: Blackhole Tracker: BHSM Boundary Interpretation of Compact-Lens Mass, Motion, and Conditional Response

authors.name: Norman P. Carberry
authors.provenance: Established author facts reused under the user's current instruction 'Thats it, the same as always'; contact and identity recovered by coordinating agent from preserved manuscripts.

abstract: Blackhole Tracker provides reproducible compact-lens inference with an explicit Berger–Hopf Standard Model (BHSM) boundary interpretation. Ordinary mass, center and motion describe one effective exterior in the adopted Einstein/GHY sector; its monopole also determines the principal extrinsic-curvature deficit and boundary energy of a declared enclosing sphere. One optical potential is counted once. A local app, command line, Python package and executed notebooks fit resolved image pairs, flux ratios and delays with full supplied covariance, nuisance profiling and explicit rejection or unresolved outcomes. In a fixed synthetic ten-year, three-source validation, all 64 noise realizations complete; nominal local 95% interval coverage is 59–61 of 64 across five mass, center and motion components. Short cosmological tracks remain motion unresolved, and omitted shear produces a rejected fit. An optional scalar–tensor realization supplies a normalized boundary-to-lensing transfer and a uniform sufficient state bound throughout its retained exterior. Frozen full-line projection erases two quadrupole modes; the leading screened primary-pair delay response vanishes; a standard apparent-mass statistic confounds the leading response with shear. The admitted nearby envelope remains below the supplied noise. These results support candidate tracking and conditional response tests. No new black-hole detection, horizon classification, physical core-transfer law or selected deformation state is established.
